strengths: Establishes a strictly symmetrical evaluation by explicitly removing any asymmetrical burden of proof.
Highly granular and fixed evidentiary classes prevent double-counting of genealogically dependent witnesses.
The universal source-risk rule (Rule 10) ensures that adjustments for bias are applied identically to all traditions and require independent behavioral evidence.
The decision threshold algorithm (Rule 12) is precise, eliminating subjective aggregations of weak evidence to declare a winner.
The reporting requirements (Rule 13), including the use of control variables and reversed labels, set an exceptionally high standard for reproducibility.
comparison_to_own_proposal: The most significant difference is the treatment of the Masoretic pointing. My independent proposal granted the received pointing a 'rebuttable presumption' and placed an asymmetrical burden of proof on the rival candidate. The author's proposal removes this presumption entirely (Rule 4), requiring both candidates to meet the exact same burden of positive evidence. While this departs from standard textual default practices, it achieves a higher degree of formal symmetry and neutrality for a blind evaluation. The author's evidentiary classes and strict decision thresholds also provide a more algorithmic, less subjective framework than my proposal's weighted tiers.
reasoning: The proposed rules are exceptionally rigorous, objective, and fair. By defining precise admissibility gates, fixed evidentiary classes, and a universal rule for handling source bias, the author has created a framework that cannot easily be manipulated to favor a predetermined outcome. The explicit removal of an asymmetrical burden of proof ensures absolute neutrality, while the requirement to freeze the protocol and audit for logical fallacies provides robust safeguards against ad hoc adjustments. The procedure is highly reproducible and clear.
